title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 42
paragraphs: So the army proceeded on its march from Lydia to the river Caïcus and the land of Mysia; and setting out from the Caïcus and keeping Mount Cane on its left, it marched through the territory of Atarneus to the city of Carene. From there it went through the plain of Thebe, passing the cities of Adramyttium and the Pelasgian Antandrus; and keeping Mount Ida on its left, it came on into the land of Ilium. When it first halted for the night close under Mount Ida, thunder and bolts of lightning fell upon it and destroyed a very great many men in that place.
